title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University (master's, Fall 2027 cohort)
organization: McGill University (Montreal, Canada), with the Mastercard Foundation
overview: Scholarships for master's degrees at McGill in nutrition, public health, public policy and sustainable agriculture for citizens and residents of African countries, the DRC included. 35 scholarships a year across 13 programmes; the page says the award covers 'all costs related to attending McGill'. The Fall 2027 cohort's application period is closed; McGill asks applicants to watch its website in Spring 2027 for the next recruitment cycle.
program_dates: Master's programmes starting in Fall 2027 (McGill 2027 cohort); the programme runs from 2024 to 2034
deadline_text: Fall 2027 cohort, as read on 2 November 2026: 'The application period for the Fall 2027 cohort is now closed.' Timeline page: mandatory information session 23 June to 15 July 2026; application August 2026 for invited applicants; 'December 1, 2026: Application deadline for candidates who received a fee waiver'; admission decisions early to mid-February 2027; scholarship selection mid-February to the beginning of March 2027. Only pre-screened applicants who received a fee waiver can still apply to McGill.
expected_next_cycle: McGill page: 'we invite you to visit our website regularly in Spring 2027 for information about the next recruitment cycle.' No dates for the next cycle are given.
funding_details: FAQ: 'The Mastercard Foundation Scholarship is comprehensive and it covers not only full tuition but all costs related to attending McGill University.' It lists: pre-arrival and immigration support; full international student tuition; on-campus housing; a personal monthly stipend; academic tools and resources
Amounts and flights are not itemised on the pages read
35 scholarships are available every year across 13 graduate programmes
participation_fee: Application fee waived for successfully pre-screened applicants
stipend: A personal monthly stipend; the amount is not stated on the pages read
eligibility: Citizen of and living in an African country (the DRC, 'Congo (Democratic Republic)', is on the list)
Has never registered for, nor completed, a master's degree
Valid passport and admissible to Canada as an international student (study permit); no dual citizenship, asylee, refugee or permanent resident status in the US, Canada, UK or EU
An exceptional record of service, leadership and activity in school or community, and a desire to give back to the home community
Financial constraints have prevented or restricted educational opportunities
35 years or younger at the time of application
A bachelor's degree in a subject closely related to the chosen programme (First Class Honours or equivalent gives a stronger chance of admission)
Priority for women, people affected by forced displacement and people living with a disability
nationality_requirements: Citizens and residents of African countries; 'Congo (Democratic Republic)' is on the eligible list
age_requirement: 35 or younger at the time of application
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree closely related to the programme; never registered for a master's
experience_requirement: An exceptional record of service and leadership; no minimum years stated
other_requirements: Eligible programmes (non-thesis): Animal Science: Sustainable Agriculture; three Bioresource Engineering streams; Biostatistics; Biotechnology; two Food Science streams; Human Nutrition: Project; Public Health; Public Policy. Thesis: Animal Science; Bioresource Engineering

Apply to the scholarship programme first; only pre-screened applicants receive a fee waiver and instructions to apply to McGill. Applications made directly to McGill are not eligible for the scholarship
application_process: Attend a mandatory information session to receive the link to the application form (2027 cohort: 23 June to 15 July 2026)
Complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form, then supply requested documents for pre-screening
Successfully pre-screened applicants receive a fee waiver and instructions to apply for admission to McGill

eligibility_reason: DRC citizenship and residence, the age limit and a bachelor's-only profile fit. The profile does not record a valid passport, a record of service and leadership, financial need, or whether a Business Administration degree is 'closely related' to the one plausible programme, Public Policy.
potential_issues: The Fall 2027 cohort is closed; the next recruitment cycle is expected in Spring 2027 with no dates yet
Only 35 awards across 13 programmes, most in agriculture, nutrition, engineering and health; Public Policy is the only evident fit for this profile
A mandatory information session comes before the application link is given out
The bachelor's degree must be 'closely related' to the programme; the DRC degree equivalence is judged by McGill
Amounts, flights, insurance and visa costs are not itemised on the pages read
benefits: Full tuition, on-campus housing and a monthly stipend at a leading Canadian university
Leadership programme and alumni network of over 200 scholars from over 20 African countries
relevance_reason: A fully funded master's that names the DRC; the Public Policy programme matches the interest in public-sector and policy analysis, but the leadership and financial-need criteria and the narrow programme list make it a stretch.

visa.support: 'Pre-arrival and immigration support' is listed; costs are not itemised

upfront_cost_risk: Low: the fee is waived for pre-screened applicants; the page warns that any non-mcgill.ca application page may be fraudulent
action: Nothing is open. Look at mcgill.ca/mastercardfdn-scholars in Spring 2027 for the next cycle and its mandatory information session, and read the Public Policy programme page first. Use only the mcgill.ca address.
notes: Found through a web search on 2 November 2026 (an aggregator quoted 1 December 2026 as a deadline; the official timeline shows it applies only to candidates who already received a fee waiver).
